python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p="hourglass/timesheet.py"
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Tuple","from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Tuple\n\nTally = Dict[str, Tuple[int, int]]",1)
s=s.replace("def _tally(shifts: Iterable[Shift]) -> Dict[str, Tuple[int, int]]:","def _tally(shifts: Iterable[Shift]) -> Tally:")
s=s.replace("        totals[shift.worker] = (count + 1, mins + shift.span.minutes)","        mins += shift.span.minutes\n        totals[shift.worker] = (count + 1, mins)")
s=s.replace("def _busiest_first(item: Tuple[str, Tuple[int, int]]):","def _busiest_first(item):")
s=s.replace('    """One line per worker, like Ana: 3 shifts, 12.5 hours."""','    """One line per worker, busiest first."""')
s=s.replace('    ranked = sorted(totals.items(), key=_busiest_first)\n    return [\n        f"{name}: {count} shifts, {mins / 60:.1f} hours"\n        for name, (count, mins) in ranked\n    ]',
'    ranked = sorted(totals.items(), key=_busiest_first)\n    return [\n        f"{name}: {count} shifts, {mins / 60:.1f} hours"\n        for name, (count, mins) in ranked\n    ]')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
sed -i 's/11 + 1/12/' tests/test_timesheet.py
awk 'length>60{print FILENAME": "FNR": "$0}' hourglass/timesheet.py tests/test_timesheet.py; make check 2>&1 | tail -4

sed -i '' 's/11 + 1/12/' tests/test_timesheet.py && awk 'length>60{print FILENAME": "FNR": "$0}' hourglass/timesheet.py tests/test_timesheet.py; make check 2>&1 | tail -4; make lint | tail -2; git add hourglass/timesheet.py tests/test_timesheet.py && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add weekly timesheet lines

Payroll needs one row per worker with shift count and total hours,
and the schedule module only exposes raw minutes per worker. This
adds timesheet_lines, which lists the busiest workers first and
rejects an empty shift list or a blank worker name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline | head -1

cat -s tests/test_timesheet.py > /tmp/ts_test.py && cp /tmp/ts_test.py tests/test_timesheet.py && make check 2>&1 | tail -3 && git add tests/test_timesheet.py && git commit -q --amend --no-edit && git status --short && git log --oneline | head -1

trace.final_message: I added `timesheet_lines` in `hourglass/timesheet.py` and committed it. It returns one line per worker, such as `Ana: two shifts, five point zero hours` but written with digits, for example `Ana: 2 shifts, 5.0 hours`. Busiest workers come first, ranked by total time, then shift count, then name. An empty list or a shift with a blank worker name raises `ProjectError`. The four new tests are in `tests/test_timesheet.py`. The full suite passes with thirty tests, and lint is clean. The commit is `bbdf1c3`. Two details you may want to change: the line always says "shifts", even for a single shift, and "busiest" means most total time, not most shifts.
